minors.title: cross-build.sh SQLCipher assert cannot fail: mesh111's own strings satisfy it
minors.why: The assert is `grep -aq 'cipher_version' && grep -aqi 'sqlcipher'` on the release binary. mesh111's non-test code already contains both strings: store/mod.rs:397 has "PRAGMA cipher_version" and store/mod.rs:72 has "SQLCipher is not linked (refusing a plaintext store)". I confirmed both strings are in libmesh111-*.rlib. Failing input: switch mesh111's rusqlite feature to `bundled`, or let the release env set LIBSQLITE3_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG / OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR. The binary then links plain SQLite and the script still prints "ok: x86_64 links SQLCipher (vendored OpenSSL)". The comment's claim that "a build that silently fell back to plain SQLite ... fails here" is not kept. Today the damage is limited: check.sh's host and x86_64-musl store tests catch a feature flip, and at runtime the store refuses to open, so the failure is closed and messaging is simply down. The only uncaught case is env drift that affects the release build alone.
minors.fix: Assert strings that only the C code carries. `cipher_plaintext_header_size` (or `sqlcipher_export`) appears only in SQLCipher's sqlite3.c, never in our sources. Also assert `OpenSSL <ver>`, taking the version from Cargo.lock's `openssl-src` `+3.6.3` suffix. I checked that all 8 aarch64 test binaries contain both. Better still, have the x86_64 release binary open, write and reopen a scratch SQLCipher store (a hidden self-test verb). Also `unset LIBSQLITE3_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR OPENSSL_DIR` and their per-target forms in cross-build.sh.

minors.title: check.sh aarch64 G2 stage prints "SQLCipher + OpenSSL linked" but never checks it
minors.where: bootstrap/scripts/check.sh (SQLCipher static link, musl aarch64 stage)
minors.why: The loop checks only three things: no INTERP, no NEEDED, and that the binary is AArch64. The echo line claims SQLCipher and OpenSSL are linked, and nothing asserts that. Right now it happens to be true: all 8 binaries contain `cipher_plaintext_header_size` and `OpenSSL 3.6.3`. But the stage would print the same line for static aarch64 binaries with plain SQLite. The x86_64 stage also asserts nothing about static linking; it relies on the musl default crt-static.
minors.fix: For each binary (or at least the mesh111 lib-test binary), add the same two string asserts proposed for cross-build.sh, and add the INTERP/NEEDED check to the x86_64 binaries too. Otherwise, reword the echo to say only what is checked.

minors.title: G2 can be skipped and check.sh still prints ALL GREEN; half-installed toolchain falls back to host cc
minors.why: §20 G2 puts the SQLCipher static builds for both targets in check.sh, and check.sh is the lock gate and the release-checklist gate. When either cross compiler is missing, both G2 stages print SKIPPED and the run still ends ALL GREEN. messaging/scripts/check.sh gates only on x86_64-linux-musl-gcc but also runs `cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`. With only the x86_64 toolchain installed, cc-rs falls back to host cc for SQLCipher and OpenSSL, and `cargo check` never links, so the aarch64 'check' passes without having built anything for aarch64. This is the silent fallback that deviation 8 says cross-build.sh prevents.
minors.fix: Export the same CC_<triple>/AR_<triple> values in both check.sh files. Identical values cause no rebuild ping-pong between workspaces. Gate messaging's musl block on both compilers. When G2 is skipped, end with something like "GREEN (G2 SKIPPED — not a lock run)" instead of ALL GREEN, or fail under CI=1 / REQUIRE_G2=1.

minors.title: Docs say the node cross-checks the Layer 5 pins; no caller does yet
minors.where: bootstrap/crates/node111/src/manifest.rs (module doc "Layer 5 entries"); bootstrap/manifest/gen-manifest.py docstring ("which the node cross-checks against these pins")
minors.why: `verify_layer5_tree` has no caller (deviation 4), so both texts describe a property the code does not have yet. The TASKS row criterion "Layer 1 updater reads them" is likewise not met.
minors.fix: Land the call sites (see the deviation 4 verdict for where), or change the wording to "will cross-check once wired (row X)".

minors.title: No CI-side check that payload contents match the Layer 5 pins; generator trusts the .tree and can emit an unparseable manifest
minors.why: Until the node call sites land, release time is the only place a mismatch can be caught. A payload packed with a different meshmud than the pinned, verdict-checked artifact, or a bundle tree that differs from the .tree, would ship unnoticed. That also breaks the GPL source-offer correspondence for meshmud. tree-sha256 is taken from the .tree file without being checked against the .tar it sits beside. pkg.meshmud is emitted for an arch whose payload-<triple>.tar.gz is absent, and node parse then refuses the whole manifest, which halts updates for every node.
minors.fix: In gen-manifest: unpack each payload-<triple>.tar.gz to a temp dir and check bin/meshmud, panels/meshtastic-web/ (recomputing the tree hash) and the presence lock against the values about to be written. Recompute the tree listing from the .tar. Refuse a meshmud whose triple has no payload. Alternatively, expose verify_layer5_tree as a `111` subcommand and call it.

minors.title: Manifest has no way to evolve; closing pkg/bundle names removes the one forward-compatible slot
minors.why: bootstrap/README says `[pkg.*.target.*]`. Before B1, an unknown package name parsed and was ignored, so new packages were forward compatible. Now pkg names are closed and bundle names closed too, the version must equal 1 exactly, and unknown sections are refused. Once the first signed release ships, any new package or bundle makes every node on this binary refuse the whole channel manifest. Examples: D19 c's manifest-pinned KISS-modem images, or a second panel (P7). Those nodes can then never update, security fixes included, and recovery is a re-anchor (manual reinstall). This trap already existed for new sections before B1; B1 extends it to package names. Closing names at parse buys almost nothing, because the manifest is signed and the tree check already refuses unpinned assets.
minors.fix: Decide before the first signed release (owner question). Option (a): keep closure in verify_layer5_tree but parse unknown pkg/bundle names and ignore them. Option (b): keep parse-time closure and amend the L1 spec with an explicit evolution path, e.g. per-version manifest files published side by side or a reader-version field. Either way, update the L1 README text that still says pkg.*.

minors.title: verify_layer5_tree checks only the last path component for links
minors.why: `symlink_metadata(tree/bin/meshmud)` follows `bin` and `share/meshtastic-presence` if those are links. With `tree/bin -> /usr/bin` and an identical meshmud there, the check passes; `ensure_absent` likewise resolves through a linked parent. The pinned bundles are also hashed before `panels/` itself is confirmed to be a real directory. None of this is reachable through the wired paths, because safe_unpack refuses symlink and hardlink entries. It is defence-in-depth only, but the doc says "never a link".
minors.fix: Run lstat on every component between `tree` and each target (bin, share, share/meshtastic-presence, panels) and refuse links. Check `panels` before hashing. Add a test with `bin` as a symlink.

minors.title: Two gate tests pass silently when their tools are missing
minors.why: If sh/find/sort/xargs/sha256sum/sed or python3 are absent, both tests `return` early and report ok. The CI tree-hash parity, which is the property that lets WEB_TREE_SHA256 verify on a node, would then go unchecked while the run shows green. Wave 1 M1 m9 made the same kind of skip visible.
minors.fix: Fail, or skip visibly (an `#[ignore]` with a reason, or an env-gated hard failure in check.sh).

minors.title: Notices: SQLCipher's licence text is not reproduced verbatim; OpenSSL line could be tighter
minors.where: bootstrap/scripts/gen-notices.py → THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md (libsqlite3-sys and openssl-src native-code notes)
minors.why: SQLCipher's LICENSE is not the generic BSD-3 text. Its clause 3 and its disclaimer name "ZETETIC LLC", while the file carries the generic text under a placeholder `<copyright holders>` line. BSD clause 2 requires binary redistributions to reproduce "this list of conditions and the following disclaimer", which means Zetetic's wording. The OpenSSL note links to LICENSE.txt on `master` rather than the shipped tag and gives no year range.
minors.fix: Have gen-notices emit libsqlite3-sys's `sqlcipher/LICENSE` verbatim, as it already does for CDLA, with "Copyright (c) 2008-2020 Zetetic LLC". OpenSSL line: "OpenSSL 3.6.3 — Copyright 1995-2026 The OpenSSL Project Authors. All Rights Reserved. Apache License 2.0 (https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.6.3/LICENSE.txt)", followed by the Apache-2.0 text that is already in the file.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 1. Bundle at panels/meshtastic-web/ (not current/panels/meshtastic/)
deviation_verdicts.why: This is the as-built path. assets/panels/meshtastic.toml, panels/static.rs and the bootstrap README L5 amendment ("unpacked ... to panels/meshtastic-web") all agree, and the brief's path would 502.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 2. manifest-version stays 1; Layer 5 sections optional
deviation_verdicts.why: No signed release has shipped, and the first one carries these sections, so no deployed binary is affected. The evolution trap this creates later is a separate minor (no evolution path).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 3. Closed pkg names {111, meshmud} and bundle names {meshtastic-web}, enforced at parse
deviation_verdicts.why: It is fail-closed, enforced in parse() (so also in parse_verified), and matches the lead's brief. Accepted on condition that the owner settles the forward-compatibility consequence before the first signed release (minor: no evolution path), and that the L1 README's `[pkg.*.target.*]` is amended to name the closed set.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 4. verify_layer5_tree implemented but not called (3 updater call sites)
deviation_verdicts.why: Integrity holds today. The payload tarball's size and sha256 come from the signed manifest and are re-checked by the root helper (update_helper.rs:154-167, which also extracts the tarball itself) and by the installer (install/stage.rs:38-44). safe_unpack refuses symlink, hardlink and device entries and `..`. So every byte of bin/meshmud, panels/ and share/meshtastic-presence/ is already authenticated by the signed manifest, and verify_layer5_tree adds only a CI-consistency cross-check and absence rules. That is enough until the call sites land. However, the row criterion "Layer 1 updater reads them" is unmet, so this must be its own row before the L5 lock. Wire it in update_helper.rs after its own safe_unpack + verify_tree (the authoritative root actor), in install/stage.rs at both verify_tree sites (the line-30 content probe would otherwise accept an existing release dir with an unpinned bin/meshmud) and the line-71 extraction, and in fetch.rs (early, advisory refusal).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 5. release-checklist not updated for bin/meshmud, panels/meshtastic-web, share/meshtastic-presence
deviation_verdicts.why: The file is outside B1's ownership. It needs a row, and that row must list the Layer 5 files in share/payload.manifest: verify_tree checks only listed files, so update_guard's torn-payload check skips unlisted Layer 5 assets.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 6. Nothing builds venvs/presence yet
deviation_verdicts.why: Out of B1's ownership. The manifest API (presence_lock, PRESENCE_LOCK, PRESENCE_VENV) is in place, and `pip install --require-hashes` fails closed on a bad hash. It needs a row, because M1's presence child has no venv to run until then.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 7. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES stale vs F2 lock; OpenSSL 3.6.3 unnamed
deviation_verdicts.why: 43c98bd resolves it. On a clean export, `gen-notices --check` reports the file current, and OpenSSL 3.6.3 is named with its Apache-2.0 pointer. The gap was never a licence breach in a gate-passing state: at 09dc397 OpenSSL was not yet linked, and between F2 and 43c98bd `--check` failed, so no release could pass the release-checklist gate. Apache-2.0 for object form needs §4(a), a copy of the licence, which the Apache-2.0 text already in the file satisfies. openssl-src's OpenSSL 3.6.3 tree has only LICENSE.txt and no NOTICE file, so §4(d) requires nothing more. §4(c) applies to Source form. The text that must appear is the component identification plus the Apache-2.0 text. A copyright line and a tag-pinned link are recommended (see minor).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 8. check.sh keeps cc-rs prefix discovery; cross-build.sh pins CC_/AR_
deviation_verdicts.why: cross-build's pinning is correct: a missing compiler is a hard error. The cost of not pinning in check.sh is covered by the G2-skip minor; pinning identical values in both scripts avoids the rebuild ping-pong.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 9. Extra check.sh stages (G2 link+run, notices tests, presence sidecar + gen_lock --verify, shellcheck)
deviation_verdicts.why: They are within §19 L1 / §20 G2 scope. gen_lock --verify is honestly labelled "structure". All of them ran green on a clean export.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 10. packageManager already pinned; package.json unchanged
deviation_verdicts.why: No change was needed.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 11. cross-build SQLCipher assert keyed on Cargo.lock listing mesh111
deviation_verdicts.why: The keying fails closed. The assert's content is the problem, not the keying; see the first minor.

result.notes:
I found no majors. The B1 code is sound: deny_unknown_fields is kept, including on RawBundle; closed names are enforced in parse(); size, sha256 and tree-sha256 are all checked; the bundle walk refuses links and specials, is bounded (65,536 files, depth 32) and has no traversal; tree-hash parity with meshtastic-web-build.sh's `tree_manifest` is tested against the real function; and the 39-crate sign-off matches Cargo.lock. Lock diff: 51 new entries = 39 compiled + mesh111 + 11 target-gated, and `cargo tree --target <musl>` confirms the 11 are never compiled. A license spot-check of 28 crates found every one matching, including foldhash (Zlib), self_cell (Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only, Apache elected), openssl-src (MIT/Apache-2.0), libsqlite3-sys (MIT) and the bundled SQLCipher 4.14.0 community on SQLite 3.51.3. No GPL, AGPL or non-OSI licence entered without an elected permissive option.

Check: I ran bootstrap/scripts/check.sh on a clean `git archive 43c98bd` export (HEAD differs only in plan/), with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/claude-1000/b1-review-target and node_modules symlinked. Result: ALL GREEN, exit 0. Notices are current; 10 of 10 manifest_layer5 tests pass; the x86_64-musl mesh111 tests ran; \"ok: 8 aarch64 test binaries\"; UI budget eager 102.8 / lazy 176.4 KB. Log: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kia-projects-111network/3a9939aa-635d-4885-a9ea-6584b070c677/scratchpad/check.log. The clean export is at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kia-projects-111network/3a9939aa-635d-4885-a9ea-6584b070c677/scratchpad/head (safe to delete, as is the target dir).

Read first:
1. The first two minors, on gate honesty. cross-build.sh's SQLCipher assert matches strings in mesh111's own code (\"PRAGMA cipher_version\" and \"SQLCipher is not linked ...\"), so it cannot detect a plain-SQLite build. check.sh's aarch64 echo claims SQLCipher and OpenSSL are linked without asserting it. Discriminating strings that work: `cipher_plaintext_header_size` and `OpenSSL 3.6.3`, both present in all 8 aarch64 test binaries and absent from our sources.
2. The deviation 4 verdict: where to wire the three call sites, plus a fourth (install/stage.rs:30's content probe).
3. The \"no way to evolve\" minor, which needs an owner decision.

What protects the Layer 5 assets today is the signed manifest's payload pin, re-hashed by the root helper and the installer, together with safe_unpack's refusal of links. That is enough for integrity until the call sites land. What is missing is the consistency check between the CI-built meshmud/bundle and the payload contents, which matters for meshmud's GPL source-offer correspondence. The cheapest place to add it now is gen-manifest.

Open questions for the owner:
(a) Manifest evolution. Exact version 1, deny_unknown_fields and closed names together mean any future package (KISS-modem images, D19 c) or second panel strands nodes on B1-era binaries. Should unknown names be tolerated at parse, or should the spec gain a dual-publish / reader-version path before the first signed release?
(b) Should check.sh refuse to print ALL GREEN when G2 is skipped, given it is both the lock gate and the release-checklist gate?
(c) Who owns the rows for the three call sites, the release checklist and the presence venv (deviations 4–6)?
The RUSTSEC-2024-0370 note on proc-macro-error is still unverified (no cargo-audit on this box) and should be re-checked in CI.

majors.title: Panel tab is silently blocked by the dashboard's own CSP when the panel is switched on after the page loaded (the usual first-run order)
majors.where: interface/ui/src/views/services/panel.tsx (Framed/PanelFrame); interacts with bootstrap/crates/node111/src/daemon/dashboard/routes.rs:85-107 (dashboard_csp, computed per document request) and daemon/panels/mod.rs:456-475 (frame_origins lists only enabled+listening panels) and panels/mod.rs:650-671 (a panel is enabled only once its service is not `unset`)
majors.why: The page's frame-src is fixed when index.html is fetched. Hash routing and SSE mean the document is almost never reloaded. Failing sequence: open http://192.168.1.42:11180/ before Meshtastic is set up. The service is `unset`, so there is no panel listener, the CSP has no frame-src, and frames fall back to default-src 'self'. Then bind the board: P1's reconcile enables the 11190 listener, a `panels` frame arrives and the service goes LIVE. Open the Panel tab: the mint succeeds and ticketSrc accepts the URL, but the iframe navigation to http://192.168.1.42:11190/?p111_ticket=… is refused by the parent's CSP. The frame shows the browser's blocked-content page and no copy explains it. Reload mints fresh tickets into the same blocked frame. The element's load event most likely still fires (Chromium), so the 30+5 s 'slow' note never shows either. Only 'Open full client' works, because it is a top-level navigation. The row's Check required a headless-chrome check of the iframe and the CSP. The CSP half was not run: the builder's hand test used vite dev, which sends no CSP, with the stub panel already listening. So this path has never been exercised. This is not a security hole (it fails closed), but the row's main deliverable does not work in the normal set-up order.
majors.fix: In Framed, add a document 'securitypolicyviolation' listener: when effectiveDirective is frame-src, child-src or default-src and the origin of blockedURI equals panelOrigin(panel, env), replace the frame with honest copy ('This page was loaded before the panel was switched on, so its security policy does not list it yet. Reload the page.') and a button that calls location.reload(). Keep Open full client. Optionally warn ahead of time for panels that were not enabled+listening in the first GET /panels. Add a test that dispatches a fake violation event. Run the row's headless-chrome iframe+CSP check against a real 111d in this exact order. Owner question: should P1 list every declared panel slot in frame-src, not only enabled ones? That would be a §13 amendment.

minors.title: Restore-pending detection never fires against the real daemon; the copy contradicts the §15 as-built
minors.where: interface/ui/src/views/settings/messaging-model.ts:196-204 (RESTORE_HELP, RESTORE_PENDING_TEXT, restorePending); messaging.tsx 'After a restore' row
minors.why: The daemon's fabric row never emits reason_code restore_pending (services/mod.rs fabric() emits fabric_off, store_failed, store_full, hub_*, peer_linked, not_enrolled). Since F2, POST /messages answers 409 restore_pending and does not queue the message (§15 as-built). So a node restored from its words has no queued own message, restorePending() is false, and the page says 'Nothing is waiting on a restore.' while the node refuses every send. RESTORE_HELP also says new messages 'stay queued … and go out by themselves', which is now false. The settings-l5 test exercises a reason_code the daemon never sends.
minors.fix: Carry FabricStore.restore_pending to F2/C1: mesh111 StoreView already has restore_pending, and fabric/json.rs status() drops it. Read that field. Until it exists, say 'not reported' rather than 'Nothing is waiting'. Reword: new messages are refused until the restore completes; ones already in the outbox wait, queued.

minors.title: Quota editor offers classes the node refuses and labels the real classes with raw ids
minors.why: The daemon's quota classes are kb, update, patch, sync, object and custody (fabric/json.rs quota_class). parse_settings rejects 'msg' (api_v1/fabric.rs test at line 428). Typing a value into 'Messages' or 'Agent operations' sends PATCH {"quotas":{"msg":…}}, which returns 400. sync, object and custody appear only as raw-id rows. The openapi FabricSettings.quotas description ('keys such as msg, agent_op, …') is the source of the drift.
minors.fix: Build the rows only from the keys in the node's settings.quotas (the daemon emits every refusable class, null when unset), with plain labels for those six classes. Carry the openapi description fix to F2/C1.

minors.title: A one-time code stays on screen after it was used or dismissed elsewhere
minors.why: Sequence: show a code; a member enrolls with it (single use, so offer_active turns false in the fabric frame), or the owner runs `111 fabric offer` or dismisses from the CLI. The card still shows the code with 'works once', which invites handing out a dead code.
minors.fix: When fabric.hub.offer_active goes from true to false after this mint, clear `offer` and say 'The code was used or dismissed.' Add a test.

minors.title: 'Never same-origin with the dashboard' rests on the daemon alone
minors.why: ticketSrc pins the frame to location.hostname plus panel.port but never checks that port. My replica run: ticketSrc('/?t', {port: 11180}, loopback) returns http://127.0.0.1:11180/?t. A record or proxy setup where panel.port equals the dashboard's port would put an allow-scripts + allow-same-origin frame on the dashboard origin, which is a full sandbox escape. Today only P1's slot block and the dashboard's frame-ancestors 'none'/XFO prevent it.
minors.fix: Refuse with bad_url unless 11190 ≤ panel.port ≤ 11229 (the contract range) and String(panel.port) differs from the dashboard's effective port. Add a test.

minors.title: Mint reply shape not checked
minors.why: A non-string url frames the panel origin at '/undefined' or '/[object%20Object]' (no ticket, so the panel's 403 page). A missing expires_in makes setTimeout(NaN), so the 'spent ticket' note appears at once. fresh() also never routes a 401 to pairing, because onError is not called there.
minors.fix: Require typeof url === 'string' and a non-empty value, else bad_url. Clamp expires_in to an integer between 1 and 300. Call deps.onError in fresh()'s failure path.

minors.title: Peer-authored hub name rendered without isolation or a length cut
minors.why: The name is the contact alias, else the hub card's label, which the peer writes. cleanPeerText strips controls and overrides, but unlike Nearby the name has no dir=auto/isolate and no cut. Plain RTL text reorders the adjacent summary, and a long label (up to the card cap) overflows the spec table at 390 px.
minors.fix: Render it in <span dir="auto" class="[unicode-bidi:isolate] break-words"> and clip it, as nearby/model.ts does (40–64 chars).

minors.title: Prune and store-full copy is narrower than §10.4 (4)
minors.why: The copy says the store never deletes '… a pinned contact' and leaves contacts out of the full-store sentence. The spec says it never deletes 'pinned items or contacts' (all contacts), so the copy implies unpinned contacts can be pruned.
minors.fix: Say: never undelivered messages, mail held for members, pending requests, pinned items, or contacts.

minors.title: §13 'dashboard re-mints' and §14 'Panel connection' copy are missing and not recorded
minors.why: The page cannot see a 403 panel_ticket_expired inside a cross-origin frame, and load fires on that page, so re-minting is manual (Reload) with no hint. §14 says the panel's honest copy gives the exact node address (the panel's own host:port) for the web client's connect dialog. That copy is not shown.
minors.fix: Under the chrome, show 'If the client asks for a node address, use <host:port>' with a copy button, and 'If the panel says its session expired, press Reload'. Record both in the README as-built note.

minors.title: Nearby: future-dated clock hints read 'just now'; a starting service's list is not marked as last known
minors.why: agoText clamps negative ages to 'just now', so a node whose clock is ahead (or hostile) always looks fresh. With the service in `starting` (uplink_waiting, node_db_pending) the daemon still serves the last snapshot (meshtastic/mod.rs nearby_sources), but nearbyState marks a list stale only when disconnected or in error.
minors.fix: Treat a hint more than about 60 s in the future as 'clock ahead of this node'. Mark the list as last known for `starting` too.

minors.title: Stale hub card rides along after a bare-code paste
minors.why: Paste bundle A, then paste or type a bare code (or another address) for hub B. `card` still holds A's card, so ENROLL is sealed to the wrong hub and fails as a confusing 502.
minors.fix: Clear `card` when a bare code is applied or the address is edited after a bundle.

minors.title: Tests: several assert the implementation or nothing; fail-closed cases are not pinned
minors.where: interface/ui/test/prompts.test.ts ('no goal sentence carries…'), test/panel-tab.test.ts ticketSrc block, test/settings-l5.test.ts bundle/restore
minors.why: The 'hostile' prompt test never puts the hostile string into the input. 'not a url at all %%%' only checks the result is not the raw string; in fact it frames http://127.0.0.1:11190/not%20a%20url…. Byte-identity of the existing prompts is compared new-against-new, not against a pre-U2 golden string. The bundle vector is not taken from mesh111 HubBundle::text(). These ticketSrc cases are unpinned: `http://127.0.0.1:11190@evil.com/`, `//evil.com:11190/`, backslash forms, the https→http rebuild, a non-string url, panel.port equal to the dashboard port. My replica run refuses or normalizes all of them correctly, so the code is right but unprotected. The CSP path has no test.
minors.fix: Add those vectors. Pin one full pre-U2 setup/fix prompt string. Inject the hostile text through status/service fields. Use a crate-generated 111HUB vector. Test the CSP violation branch from the major.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: /settings/l5 reachable in Simple mode (SIMPLE_LAYER_PAGE, no minMode, no advanced badge)
deviation_verdicts.why: §16 does not give the page a mode. Enrolling is the first step of the core Messages view, and the Messages banner now links there. Rows that change the node stay loopback-gated, and the change can be reverted with one conditional. It does amend interface README §6.7 (Layer 4, locked: '/settings/l0..l9 (advanced)'), so the owner should confirm it before L5 locks.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: LAYERS[5].title 'Messaging' -> 'Messaging & data' (+ description)
deviation_verdicts.why: §16 names the page 'Settings → Messaging & Data'. layers.ts is in U2's ownership, and the shell test was updated to match.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: No literal relayed/queued placeholders; U1's STATE_COPY reused as the fabric page legend
deviation_verdicts.why: I checked STATE_COPY against §9: queued (no path, key missing, their hub is not yours) and relayed ('A mailbox node saved it and will hold it for them.') match. Reusing it keeps one source of the copy.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Loopback-only panels handled reactively (403 loopback_only from the mint, no frame)
deviation_verdicts.why: Verified in P1's api_v1/panels.rs: MintError::LoopbackOnly answers 403 loopback_only, and the contract Panel has no auth-mode field. The refusal fails closed: no frame, honest copy and the loopback URL. An optional Panel.auth_mode would let the page show this before minting; carry that to F2/C1 if wanted.

majors.title: Restore-pending (RestoreFloorRequired) is silently converted into a counter reset: shutdown and inbound observation persist a counters file with announce_last = 0
majors.where: bootstrap/crates/node111/src/daemon/fabric/sealer.rs `IdentitySealer::shutdown_counters` (called unconditionally from `FabricHandle::shutdown` and from `boot()`'s error path in fabric/mod.rs) and `boot_with` in fabric/mod.rs (registers tcp-lan whenever `ensure_announce` is not `Missing`, i.e. also while `restore_pending()`)
majors.why: id111 `CounterStore::restore_pending()` keeps announce_last = 0 / traffic_base = 0 in memory and writes no file; its `shutdown()`, `commit()` and `persist()` carry no restore-pending guard and the file format has no pending flag. F2 calls `shutdown()` on every clean stop, so a daemon that started without `identity/counters` writes `{clean, announce_last 0, traffic_base 0}` at its first orderly stop. Next start: `CounterStore::open` → `CounterOpen::Present`, `restore_pending() == false`, `next_announce_counter()` → 1: `ensure_announce` mints an announce with counter 1 and `Fabric::start` mints epoch 2 — with a kept store.db whose recorded epoch is higher the fabric fails `EpochNotIncreasing` and stays down with no repair path; with a fresh store the node's msg_seq epochs restart from 2 and every peer that still holds rx_state / rx_floor for this NodeId treats the new (epoch, n) as already-delivered duplicates (§4: 'below a prefix nothing is ever forgotten') — silent message loss, the exact A3 collision the floor exists to prevent. `111 identity restore` can no longer set a floor (`restore_pending(dir)` → AlreadyExists; the CLI also refuses a live identity). Reproduced against id111 directly (scratch program /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kia-projects-111network/3a9939aa-635d-4885-a9ea-6584b070c677/scratchpad/rp-check/src/main.rs): shutdown-in-pending writes the file; next open reports is_restore_pending=false, announce_last=0, issues counter 1; restore_pending(dir) → AlreadyExists. Second trigger, no shutdown needed: with a valid `fabric/announce` on disk (same keys, matching appdata) `ensure_announce` returns `Kept` while pending, tcp-lan starts and a Cat 4 default binds :11183; every pair_mac-verified inbound packet goes through `observe_counter` → `tick_and_maybe_commit` → after 64 packets `commit()` writes the same file (and with an empty window every replayed packet is judged Fresh, so attribution/card answers/pushes are granted to replays — the exposure §4 accepts only because nothing is sealed). Reachability stated honestly: `111 identity restore` persists a provisional floor (announce 1024), so this needs `identity/counters` absent at daemon start (partial identity-dir copy, a hand-removed file, or following tests/README's own 'delete identity/counters' instruction) — but that is precisely the state F2 documents, logs and tests as supported, and once entered the protection is destroyed instead of held. The integration test `restore_pending_answers_409_and_seals_nothing` ends with `r.fabric.shutdown()` and never inspects the identity dir, so it passes while writing the bad file.
majors.fix: (1) `shutdown_counters()` returns Ok without persisting while `is_restore_pending()`; same guard on the `boot()` error path. (2) While `restore_pending()`, treat the stored announce as `Missing` for link purposes: do not register tcp-lan, do not bind, do not `maintain` peers (so `observe_counter` can never run); keep `own_announce()` empty so offer/card keep answering 409 restore_pending. (3) Test: drop `counters`, start with a pre-existing valid `fabric/announce`, assert `tcp()` is None, shutdown, assert `identity/counters` does not exist and `CounterStore::restore_pending(dir)` still succeeds. (4) Hand the id111 owners (I1/C5) a hardening ask: `persist`/`commit`/`shutdown` refuse or no-op while `restore_pending` (§8.4 'no file is written until then'), so no future host can repeat this.

minors.title: Dial targets accept unspecified / multicast / broadcast literals
minors.where: api_v1/fabric.rs `parse_hub_addr` (accepts any `SocketAddr` literal with port != 0) and fabric/settings.rs `decode` (`peers[].address`, `home_hub.address`)
minors.why: `0.0.0.0:11183` or `[::]:11183` parses as an IP literal; on Linux a connect to 0.0.0.0 reaches the node itself. tcp-lan's `refuse_loopback` only catches `is_loopback()` (true for 127/8 and ::1, false for 0.0.0.0), so the dialer connects to its own listener, the accept side refuses the loopback remote, and `maintain` retries forever with back-off. Multicast/broadcast targets are pointless dials kept alive the same way.
minors.fix: Refuse `is_unspecified()`, `is_multicast()`, IPv4 `is_broadcast()` (and `is_loopback()` whenever the production `refuse_loopback` is on) in `parse_hub_addr` (400 with the host:port hint) and in `settings::decode` (invalid ⇒ everything off, as today); unit-test `0.0.0.0:11183`, `[::]:11183`, `224.0.0.1:11183`, `255.255.255.255:11183`.

minors.title: Enrollment's home_hub is persisted only through the asynchronous Settings event
minors.where: api_v1/fabric.rs `enroll` (answers 200 after `f.enroll()` Ok) vs fabric/mod.rs `publish` → `on_settings` (writes fabric/settings from the SSE pump)
minors.why: The hub records the member as enrolled and the member's store holds the contact as `enrolled`, but `home_hub` lives only in `fabric/settings`, written later by the pump. A crash or pump lag between ENROLL_OK and that write leaves a member with no home hub at the next start (nothing dials, messages stay queued) while the hub considers it enrolled; the member must obtain a fresh offer to recover.
minors.fix: After `f.enroll()` returns Ok, call `h.on_settings(f.settings().await?)` (exactly as `patch_settings` already does) before answering; keep the event path as the second writer.

minors.title: A corrupt or oversize fabric/settings silently drops home_hub and peers
minors.why: Fail-closed for `hub_role`/`listen_lan`/`custody_opt_in` is right, but `home_hub: None` means the member forgets its hub on a one-byte corruption; the next settings event then overwrites the file with the hub gone, making the loss permanent while the store still says the contact is `enrolled`.
minors.fix: Move the bad file aside (`settings.invalid-<n>`) and log its path once; and/or reconstruct `home_hub` from the store's `enrolled` contact (there is exactly one in v1) when the file is absent or invalid, keeping the three booleans off.

minors.title: CLI: single-use enrollment code on argv; dechunk can panic on a multibyte boundary
minors.why: The code is a secret until spent (it survives failed attempts up to the lockout) and argv is visible in `ps` and shell history on the member. `dechunk` slices a `String` produced by `from_utf8_lossy` at a byte offset taken from the chunk-size line; a non-ASCII problem+json body (an alias, an em dash) sent chunked would panic the client. Latent today because axum's `Json` answers carry Content-Length, but the brief asks for no panics on input.
minors.fix: Read a bare code from the TTY (`read_hidden`-style) when no bundle is given and document that the bundle on argv is for a scanned QR; in `dechunk` operate on bytes or use `after.get(..n)` and stop on a miss.

minors.title: Contract responses the as-built routes answer but openapi.yaml does not list

minors.why: If the decision file cannot be written after the store committed the message, the in-memory guard stops a retried accept from sending twice — until the daemon restarts, after which the same accept sends a second message. Rare (needs a write failure on the agent dir), but the builder's 'never sent twice' claim is process-scoped and the module doc does not say so.
minors.fix: Either write the decision file first with `applied: {pending: true}` and finalize after the send (a crash then leaves a visibly half-applied proposal instead of a double send), or state the restart gap in the module doc and the README note.

result.notes:
Read first: the major — the sequence is concrete and reproduced (scratch program at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kia-projects-111network/3a9939aa-635d-4885-a9ea-6584b070c677/scratchpad/rp-check/src/main.rs: `CounterStore::restore_pending` → `shutdown()` writes the file; next `open()` reports is_restore_pending=false, announce_last=0, issues 1; `restore_pending(dir)` → AlreadyExists). The F2-side fix is small (guard `shutdown_counters` on both call sites; no tcp-lan while `restore_pending()`; one test), and id111 should get the matching `persist` guard so no host can repeat it. Then m2/m3 (home_hub lives only in fabric/settings and is written asynchronously), then the contract follow-ups (m5) for the regen pass.

What is sound (checked, no finding): the Sealer as crypto code — `store_secret` is keyed BLAKE2b over `Keyset::to_bytes()[32..64]`, which is already `Zeroizing<[u8;64]>`, the KAT is independently derived (RFC 7693 keyed mode) and the private bytes never leave the handle; `seal_payload` forwards the caller's closure to id111's FnOnce path (called exactly once with the real epk, plaintext zeroized after AEAD); `open_payload` returns the AD-verified header + epk; `sign` → `sign_with_tag` (tag prepended); `observe_counter` relays id111's A11 verdict and a Stale counter touches nothing (it is ≤ high-water by construction); `next_announce_counter` is id111's sync-commit path and errors under RestoreFloorRequired; `random` is getrandom with a typed failure; pair keys cached in `Zeroizing`, both directions dropped on forget, cache bounded at 4096 by clearing; Debug impls print node_id only; no key bytes in any Problem detail or log. Store open: Mode S via `ModeS::new(Zeroizing<secret>)` consumed inside `spawn_blocking` (no long-lived String), fabric/ 0700, announce/settings/display-times 0600, statvfs DiskSpace, `complete_partials` in `Core::recover`, clean record via `Fabric::shutdown` then counters clean. Listener: `0.0.0.0:11183` matches the dashboard's own LAN binding (bind.rs: 'The LAN listener is IPv4 0.0.0.0 only'), bound only when hub_role || listen_lan and reconciled before the PATCH answers. Routes: `require_session` bearer rule (loopback peer + minted token) then `refuse_bearer` on every write incl. message-proposal decisions; `LoopbackOnly` on settings/offer/dismiss; 202 vs 409 restore_pending via `FabricError::RestorePending`; SSE coalesced per message per batch with the current view fetched after coalescing; Last-Event-ID replay untouched (existing ring). Proposal acceptance parses the A1 body strictly (`get(..64)` cannot panic on a multibyte boundary; `\r\n`, empty text, upper-case hex, missing blank line all refused — unit matrix), stamp must equal this node, pending requests refused, applied only after `fabric.send` returned (store commit FULL). The `0.0.0.0`/loopback self-dial is closed on the accept side by `refuse_loopback` in production (m1 is about the retry loop, not a hole).

Checks I ran: `cargo test -p node111 --lib daemon::fabric` → 19 passed; `cargo test -p node111 --test api_v1_messages` → 7 passed (2.0 s) under the warm CARGO_TARGET_DIR; `pnpm run gen:types -- --check` → exit 0 with a clean working tree afterwards; `pnpm test` → 35 files / 1065 tests passed. I did not re-run clippy/musl/notices (the lead's run and 43c98bd cover them; the builder's logs are in the scratchpad).

Wave 1 standing calls respected: ignore = client-side fold (not touched), bearer never mints panel tickets (not touched), RestorePending ⇒ 409 on new sends while an already-queued item carries reason restore_pending (both consistent with the contract text), not_enrolled/cancelled in the emitted set.

Open questions for the owner: (1) Layer 2 floor discipline under Layer 5: the words-only `111 identity restore` persists a provisional floor of 1024 and the daemon then announces and mints epochs from 1025 — the §8.4 'MUST NOT announce until the floor is learned' has no enforcement now that L5 mints an epoch per store open; is a `111 identity floor <n>` (or a learned-from-hub floor) a Wave 3 item? (2) Should the contract add 409 to offerHub (yes, additive) and the three decision outcomes for message proposals? (3) U2's Settings page offers `msg`/`agent_op` quota boxes the daemon refuses — bounce U2's QUOTA_CLASSES to the six refusable classes. (4) Home hub by name vs IP is fine for v1; note it in §21 if the owner wants names later.
